messages.subject: [statnet_help] nested homophily terms
messages.body_plain:
Hi Kevin,

I'll take a stab at your first question, and parts of your second. For the 
remainder, I'll need to defer to those more knowledgeable about the 
details of the fitting algorithms. (Dave? Mark? Carter? Other statnet 
users with similar experiences?)

> question 1: is it possible to model these (nested) attributes in the 
> first place? discerning the role of ethnic homophily while controlling 
> for racial homophily, and vice versa? i have talked to several people 
> about this issue. on one hand, some have told me that i must leave out a 
> 'reference group' for each in order for the model to work. on the other 
> hand, others have told me it is ok to just go ahead and throw both 
> attributes into the model- and my preliminary results seem to confirm 
> that this is in fact works just fine, and i get intelligible results 
> (see 'model 1', attached).

If I understand your scenario correctly, then it should be fine to fit 
this model.  You would only need a reference group when all of your 
homophilous dyad types are constrained to sum to a function of another 
term in the model, but that is not the case.  (In contrast, if you have an 
edges term and a nodefactor term in the same model, then statnet will 
force a reference group, since the sum of all the nodefactor statistics 
must equal twice the number of edges.)

I imagine you might be interested in separating out the different 
ethnicities; that is, running a race-only model, and then running a model 
with race and *one* of the races broken down by ethnicity, to see how the 
likelihood changes.  To do this, you would need to code up a number of 
dummy variables out of your ethnicity variable; the first would have 
values 10, 11, and one value only for each of the remaining races; and so 
on.

> question 2: assuming that i am doing this right- i.e. that model 1 is ok- i 
> run into another problem further down the line. you'll note that in model 1, 
> statnet appropriately dropped the homophily terms for ethnicity 40 and 60- 
> because, as mentioned above, these categories are duplicates of race 4 and 
> race 6, respectively. however, something seems to go wrong when i switch over 
> to a dyad-dependence model. when i add a "mutual" term for reciprocal ties, 
> three bad things happen (see 'model 2', attached). first, i do not receive 
> MCMC s.e. statistics (i assume i should be receiving these because i am now 
> in dyad-dependence land, which is no longer equivalent to pseudo-likelihood 
> estimation). second, some of my p-values shoot way up such that fewer terms 
> are significant. and third, the homophily terms for ethnicity 40 and 60 are 
> now maintained, when they should be dropped. what am i doing wrong here? i 
> wonder if problems 1 and 2 are the result of problem 3, because the model is 
> keeping terms it shouldn't be keeping. if this is so, how do i get statnet to 
> drop these duplicate terms again?

I am not surpised that some of your p-values would go up; some of what 
seemed like strong homophily before can now be seen to be moderate 
homophily combined with mutuality, so the strength of the homophily 
predictor shoud go down.  However, your values do go up much more than I 
would have expected.  I suspect the non-dropping of the two terms may play 
some role in this.

Regarding the lack of MCMC s.e., I have no idea what that's about, so will 
need to defer to others.

Regarding the non-dropping of terms - note that there are different types 
of dropping.  ergm literally drops terms from the model altogether (i.e. 
the user is given a warning message that the term is being dropped, and it 
does not appear in the resulting list of coefficients at all) when the 
model statistic lies on the boundary or is undefined, and will yield a 
non-finite estimate.  Examples are a nodefactor term in which there are no 
ties for anyone in that attribute class; or a nodematch term for an 
attribute class containing only one node.  This is different from the 
scenario when one term is masked by another, as is the case with your data 
and model.  The glm routines in R are smart enough to be able to identify 
this, and remove one term from the fitting process, yielding a lack of 
estimate for it.  My understanding is that the MCMC fitting algorithms in 
ergm do not check for this situation.  (Or rather, they do in the 
straightforward case of a nodefactor summing up to edges, and create a 
reference group; but not in other cases, where there is masking across 
different attributes).  So the reason this worked in the first case is 
that as a dyadic independence model, the fit drew on R's glm routines and 
the masked terms were not fit, and in the latter case it went to the MCMC 
routines, which attempted to fit them and had problems. I do suspect that 
all three of your problems may actually stem from this one, although I'm 
not sure.

In terms of a solution, I imagine there is again some way to break your 
variables up into additional dummy variables, although the exact method 
for this is not clear to me right now. On the other hand, it might be 
worthwhile for us to consider adding similar checks to the MCMC algorithm 
as exist for glm, but that's a much much slower process. Anyone else have 
an idea?

Cheers,
Steve

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] more problems getting statnet to work
messages.body_plain:
Matt,

This is a problem that has beset macs.  The first thing you should do is 
check to see that you have gcc installed.  Open Terminal.app and cd to 
/usr/local/.  Is there a gcc4.0 folder?  If there isn't, that would 
explain your error!

Mac's XCode used to not work for building R and so Mac distributions of 
R included their own gcc.  As of R 2.5, gcc was no longer included in 
the R distribution. There is a discussion of this here:

http://cran.r-project.org/bin/macosx/RMacOSX-FAQ.html#Why-do-I-need-custom-compilers-for-the-CRAN-binary_003f

I think that the statnet code is written assuming that gcc was installed 
by R and the paths referred to in the code have not been changed to 
reflect the fact that XCode now works for building R.

As a temporary work-around, you can do a custom install of R 2.4, 
installing only gcc.  This should work until the code for macs is updated.

I hope this helps.

jhj
